Thanks for the screenshot — I can see what's happening. Apologies for the confusion.

Short explanation: when an invite is forwarded between Google accounts that have different timezone or locale defaults, some clients treat it as a 'floating' event (no explicit zone) and that can shift the displayed time when DST or region rules differ. The quick remedies that should resolve it are:

1) I'll reissue a fresh invite and explicitly set the event timezone to Europe/London (BST) in the event settings instead of relying on the sender's local timezone.
2) I will include an attached .ics that has the TZID property and a plain-text list of equivalent times in BST / PDT / SGT.
3) If anyone still sees a shifted time, please accept from the email with the new invite rather than from a forwarded copy — forwarded copies often lose the timezone block.

Next steps: I'm sending a corrected invite now (subject: Redwood demo — Tue Apr 14, 10:30 BST). Please accept that one; it has an explicit timezone and an ICS that includes the VTIMEZONE block. If you prefer Wed 15 at 09:00 BST instead I can swap it and send another invite.

CC'ing David who will join to cover our APAC routing recommendations in case you want the 17:30 SGT slot.

Thanks again for flagging this — will follow up once the new invite is out.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
